parts.title: Hiring a van for a house move

turns.text: Good morning, Kingsway Van Hire, Simon speaking. How can I help?
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: Oh, hi. I'm moving into a new flat next weekend, and I'd like to hire a van, please.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Lovely. Let me just take a few details first. Could I have your name?
turns.speaker: staff

turns.say: Yes, it's Megan Holroyd. Holroyd is H, O, L, R, O, Y, D.
turns.text: Yes, it's Megan Holroyd. Holroyd is H-O-L-R-O-Y-D.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Thanks, Megan. And what size van were you thinking of? We've got small, medium and large.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: Well, I was going to go for the small one, because it's only a one-bedroom flat. But I've got a sofa and a double bed, so I'm not sure they'd fit.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Honestly, with a sofa and a bed, the small one would be a real squeeze. The next size up has a much longer loading space, and it's still easy to drive. The large one's really for moving a whole house.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: Right. I'll take your advice and go for the medium one, then.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Good choice. And when would you like to pick it up?
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: I was hoping for Friday evening, but my friend who's helping me can't get off work, so it'll have to be Saturday morning.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: That's no problem, we've still got medium vans free that weekend. What time would suit you?
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: As early as possible, really. Do you open at eight?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: The office opens at eight, yes, but every van has to be checked and cleaned first. So the earliest you can collect it is 8.30.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: OK, 8.30 it is. That still gives us most of the day.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Great. Now, we also need the address you're moving to, for our insurance.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.say: It's Flat 4, 27 Lindley Road. That's L, I, N, D, L, E, Y.
turns.text: It's Flat 4, 27 Lindley Road. That's L-I-N-D-L-E-Y.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Thank you. Is that the one near the hospital?
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: That's right, just behind it. It's only about ten minutes from my old place, actually.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Handy. And could I have a contact number, in case we need to get hold of you?
turns.speaker: staff

turns.say: Yes, my mobile is oh seven seven oh oh, nine oh oh, three two six. Oh, sorry, I always mix that up. The last part is 362.
turns.text: Yes, my mobile is 07700 900 326. Oh, sorry, I always mix that up. The last part is 362.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: So that's oh seven seven oh oh, nine oh oh, three six two. Got it.
turns.text: So that's 07700 900 362. Got it.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.say: Now, how much will it cost? I saw on your website that the medium van was sixty-five pounds a day.
turns.text: Now, how much will it cost? I saw on your website that the medium van was £65 a day.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: That's our weekday price, I'm afraid. At weekends it's a bit more, so it'd be seventy-five pounds for the Saturday. But if you keep it until Sunday, we do a special deal.
turns.text: That's our weekday price, I'm afraid. At weekends it's a bit more, so it'd be £75 for the Saturday. But if you keep it until Sunday, we do a special deal.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: Actually, I might need it on Sunday as well, to take some old furniture to the tip.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: In that case, the weekend rate is one hundred and ten pounds for both days, which works out cheaper than paying for two separate days.
turns.text: In that case, the weekend rate is £110 for both days, which works out cheaper than paying for two separate days.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: Right, that sounds fine. Let's do that.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: Lovely. Would you like any extras? We hire out trolleys for eight pounds, and furniture blankets for five pounds.
turns.text: Lovely. Would you like any extras? We hire out trolleys for £8, and furniture blankets for £5.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: I've already borrowed a trolley from my neighbour, so I won't need one. But the blankets would be useful. I don't want to scratch anything.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: I'll add those to the booking. Now, there's also a deposit, which you get back when the van's returned without any damage. It used to be two hundred pounds, but it's now one hundred and fifty pounds.
turns.text: I'll add those to the booking. Now, there's also a deposit, which you get back when the van's returned without any damage. It used to be £200, but it's now £150.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: OK, that's not too bad. And what do I need to bring with me when I collect it?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Your driving licence, obviously, and something with your address on it. A bank statement isn't enough, I'm afraid. It needs to be a recent bill, like gas or electricity.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: Oh, but it'll still have my old address on it. Is that a problem?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: No, that's fine, as long as it matches the address on your licence.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: Good. And how long does it all take at the office? I don't want my friend waiting around.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: Most people expect it to take about ten minutes, but with the checks and the photos of the van, you should allow about twenty minutes.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: Twenty. OK, I'll tell her. And when I bring it back on Sunday, is there anything I need to do?
turns.speaker: caller

turns.say: You'll need to return it by six in the evening. And please make sure the tank's full before you drop it off, otherwise there's a thirty pounds refuelling charge.
turns.text: You'll need to return it by six in the evening. And please make sure the tank's full before you drop it off, otherwise there's a £30 refuelling charge.
turns.speaker: staff

turns.text: Right, I'll stop at the petrol station on the way. Thanks so much for your help.
turns.speaker: caller

turns.text: You're welcome, Megan. Good luck with the move.
turns.speaker: staff

explanation.uk: Офіс відчиняється о восьмій, але фургони спершу треба перевірити й почистити, тож забрати його вона зможе о "8.30", а не о "eight".

segments.text: Part 2. You will hear a volunteer guide welcoming a group of visitors to a botanic garden. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15.
That is the end of Part 2. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers.

parts.title: Welcome to Riverbend Botanic Gardens

turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Riverbend Botanic Gardens. My name's Aroha Tremain, and I'm one of the volunteer guides here. Before you head off on your own, I'll quickly explain where everything is, and then I'll tell you what's on this month. You've each got a map, so have a look at that as I go.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: Right. We're standing at the main gate, at the bottom of your map. The main path runs straight north from here, right up through the middle of the gardens. As you walk up it, the first building on your right is the Visitor Centre. That's where you'll find information and our gift shop.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: Now, a lot of people assume the café's in the Visitor Centre too, but it isn't. It's directly across the path from it, on your left as you walk north, right next to the Rose Garden. They do a lovely flat white, if you need one.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: Keep going and you'll reach a crossroads, where a second path runs from east to west. Now, the toilets. If you turn right at the crossroads and walk all the way to the end of that path, they're on your right-hand side. They're the only toilets in the gardens, by the way, so it's worth remembering where they are.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: On the other side of the path, facing the toilets, is the herb garden. It's a favourite with keen cooks, and you're welcome to touch and smell the plants. Just please don't pick them!
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: Okay, back to the crossroads. If you carry straight on north, the building immediately on your left is the Fernery. It's cool and shady in there, so it's a nice escape on a warm day. The building opposite it, on the right, is the staff office, and I'm afraid that's not open to visitors.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: If you've got children with you, they'll want the children's garden. For that, go to the crossroads and turn left, so you're heading west. Walk to the very end of the path, and it's on your right, just south of the Duck Pond. There's a sandpit and a little hedge maze in there.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: Last one. The plant shop sells seedlings grown in our own nursery, and it's well worth a visit. Go right to the top of the main path, where you'll see the big Glasshouse. The shop's in the small building just to the east of it, so that's on your right as you face the Glasshouse.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: Right, so that's where everything is. Now, what's on this month. We run free guided walks every day. They used to leave at 10:30 am, but this month they start at 11 am, from just outside the Visitor Centre. Do try to get there ten minutes early, though, because they fill up fast.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: In the Glasshouse, we'd planned to have our orchid display this month, but the orchids are flowering late this year, so that's been moved to January. Instead, there's a special exhibition of carnivorous plants, the ones that trap insects. The cactus collection's in there all year round, of course.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: A few people have asked about the Rose Garden. It's open as usual, but don't expect too much just yet. Most of the roses are still in bud, and they won't be at their best until about mid-December.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: Now, this Saturday there's a gardening workshop. Lots of people ask us about pruning, but we do that one in winter. This one's all about growing vegetables from seed, and everyone takes home a tray of seedlings. Next month's workshop is on composting, if that's more your thing.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.say: It's fifteen dollars per person, and there are only twenty places. Please don't try to book on our website, because the booking form isn't working this week. We can't take bookings over the phone, either. Just pop into the Visitor Centre and put your name down at the desk.
turns.text: It's $15 per person, and there are only twenty places. Please don't try to book on our website, because the booking form isn't working this week. We can't take bookings over the phone, either. Just pop into the Visitor Centre and put your name down at the desk.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: And finally, on Sunday, sorry, Friday evening, there's a twilight concert on the lawn by the Duck Pond. You don't need to bring chairs, we've got plenty, and the paths will be lit, so leave your torch at home. But it does get chilly once the sun goes down, so bring an extra layer.
turns.speaker: guide

turns.text: Okay, that's all from me. Enjoy your visit, and if you've got any questions, come and find me. I'll be by the café.
turns.speaker: guide

questions.prompt: Café
questions.evidence: It's directly across the path from it, on your left as you walk north, right next to the Rose Garden.

explanation.en: The café is not inside the Visitor Centre. It is opposite it, on the left as you walk north from the gate, next to the Rose Garden.
explanation.ru: Кафе находится не внутри "Visitor Centre", а напротив него: слева, если идти от ворот на север, рядом с "Rose Garden".
explanation.uk: Кафе розташоване не всередині "Visitor Centre", а навпроти нього: ліворуч, якщо йти від воріт на північ, поруч із "Rose Garden".

questions.prompt: Toilets
questions.evidence: turn right at the crossroads and walk all the way to the end of that path, they're on your right-hand side

explanation.en: Turning right at the crossroads means walking east. At the end of the path, the right-hand side is the south side, so the toilets are B, not the building on the north side.
explanation.ru: Повернуть направо на перекрёстке значит идти на восток. В конце дорожки правая сторона — южная, поэтому туалеты — это B, а не здание на северной стороне.
explanation.uk: Повернути праворуч на перехресті означає йти на схід. Наприкінці доріжки права сторона — південна, тож туалети — це B, а не будівля на північному боці.

questions.prompt: Herb garden
questions.evidence: On the other side of the path, facing the toilets, is the herb garden.

explanation.en: The herb garden is opposite the toilets, on the north side of the east end of the cross path.
explanation.ru: Сад пряных трав находится напротив туалетов, на северной стороне восточного конца поперечной дорожки.
explanation.uk: Сад пряних трав розташований навпроти туалетів, на північному боці східного кінця поперечної доріжки.

questions.prompt: Fernery
questions.evidence: If you carry straight on north, the building immediately on your left is the Fernery.

explanation.en: Going straight on north from the crossroads, the left side is west, so the Fernery is C. The building on the right is the staff office.
explanation.ru: Если от перекрёстка идти прямо на север, слева будет запад, поэтому "Fernery" — это C. Здание справа — служебный офис персонала.
explanation.uk: Якщо від перехрестя йти прямо на північ, ліворуч буде захід, тому "Fernery" — це C. Будівля праворуч — службовий офіс персоналу.

questions.prompt: Children's garden
questions.evidence: Walk to the very end of the path, and it's on your right, just south of the Duck Pond.

explanation.en: Turning left at the crossroads means walking west. At the very end, on the right (north) side and just below the Duck Pond, is the children's garden. You pass the Fernery on the way, but that is not at the end.
explanation.ru: Повернуть налево на перекрёстке значит идти на запад. В самом конце, справа (с северной стороны), прямо под "Duck Pond", находится детский сад-парк для детей. По пути вы проходите мимо "Fernery", но это ещё не конец дорожки.
explanation.uk: Повернути ліворуч на перехресті означає йти на захід. У самому кінці, праворуч (з північного боку), одразу під "Duck Pond", розташований сад для дітей. Дорогою ви проходите повз "Fernery", але це ще не кінець доріжки.

parts.title: Planning a student travel survey

turns.text: Come in, Shannon, Mitchell. Have a seat. So, this is your survey on how students travel to campus. Remind me why you settled on that topic?
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: Well, we both drive in from out past Penrith, so we know the problem first-hand. But honestly, that wasn't the main reason.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: No. The main thing was that the uni's deciding at the moment whether to build another multi-storey car park or spend the money on a shuttle bus, and we thought our results might actually feed into that.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: That's a good motivation. There's already plenty of research on student travel, so a link to a real decision helps. Now, you ran a pilot. How did that go?
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: Better than we expected in some ways. We were worried the wording would confuse people, but nobody asked us what anything meant.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: The real problem was the time. It took most people about twelve minutes, and a couple just gave up halfway through.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: Twelve minutes is a lot to ask of someone between lectures. So you cut it down?
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: Yes, from twenty-two questions to fourteen. It's about five minutes now.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: Good. And how have you been finding participants?
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: We started by standing outside the library with a clipboard, but that was pretty slow. We only got fifteen or so in two afternoons.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: We also asked a few lecturers to mention it at the start of class, but they said they weren't allowed to. So in the end we put a link on the student union's online noticeboard, and that's where nearly all our responses have come from.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: I see. And how many have you got so far?
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: We set ourselves a target of 150. Last Friday we had about 60, and now we're up to 110.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: That's healthy. But I do have a concern about who's answering. Have you looked at the breakdown?
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: We checked faculties, and it's a fairly even spread. Science, arts, business, all roughly the same. And we left out anyone living in the residential colleges, since they don't really travel.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: Sensible. But think about who reads the union noticeboard. It's mostly full-time students who are on campus every day. People studying part-time, often in the evenings, are hardly represented at all, and they're the group most likely to drive in after work.
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.say: Right, that's true. We've only got about six part-timers. Could we offer a prize? Like a draw for a one hundred dollars voucher?
turns.text: Right, that's true. We've only got about six part-timers. Could we offer a prize? Like a draw for a $100 voucher?
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.text: You could, but it would have to go back through the ethics committee, and that can take a month. You haven't got that long.
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: What about handing out paper copies in the car park in the evening?
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: I wouldn't. People are tired and in a hurry, and you'd need permission from campus security. The simplest thing is to email the coordinators of the evening courses and ask them to forward the link to their students.
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: Okay, we'll do that this week.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: Right. Now, I've been through your fourteen questions, and I've got a few suggestions. The first one asks for their main way of getting here, and they tick one box. But lots of people catch a train and then cycle from the station, or drive to a park-and-ride.
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: So we should add more options to the list?
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: No, your list's fine as it is. The issue is that people need to be able to tick more than one.
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: Okay. Then there's the one on weekly travel costs.
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.say: Yes. You ask for an exact dollar amount, and I suspect most people have no idea what they spend. Give them bands instead, say under twenty dollars, twenty dollars to forty dollars, and so on.
turns.text: Yes. You ask for an exact dollar amount, and I suspect most people have no idea what they spend. Give them bands instead, say under $20, $20 to $40, and so on.
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: What about postcode? A few people in the pilot didn't like giving it, so we thought about dropping it altogether.
turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: Don't drop it. It's the only way you'll be able to map where people come from. Just make it optional, so nobody feels pressured.
turns.speaker: tutor

turns.text: And the question on why people chose their transport?
turns.speaker: student_b

turns.speaker: student_a

turns.text: Exactly. Send me the revised version by Friday, and we'll meet again next week.

segments.text: Part 4. You will hear a university lecturer giving a talk about how honeybees communicate where food can be found. First, you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
That is the end of Part 4. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers.

parts.title: How honeybees share the location of food

turns.text: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to look at a question that puzzled people for a very long time: how does a honeybee that's found food tell the rest of the colony where it is? The answer, or most of it anyway, is a behavior called the waggle dance. And at the end we'll look at the limits of that idea, because it's not quite as neat as the textbooks suggest.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Let's start with Karl von Frisch, the Austrian biologist who did the classic work on this. He wanted to control exactly where the bees found food, and real flowers are very hard to control. So instead he trained bees to visit a small dish of sugar water, which he could move around the countryside wherever he liked.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Of course, he needed to know which bee was which. He considered clipping a tiny piece off their wings, but that would've changed the way they flew. So he marked each visitor with a little dot of paint, using different colors in a kind of code.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Then he watched what those bees did back home. A normal hive is dark and closed, so he used what's called an observation hive. That's basically a frame of comb with glass sides, so you can see what's going on inside without disturbing anyone.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: What he saw were two different dances. If the food was close to the hive, within about fifty meters, the returning bee ran around in small circles, first one way, then the other. He called this the round dance. It basically says, there's food nearby, go and look, without giving much detail.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: For food farther away, the bee performs the waggle dance. She runs in a straight line, shaking her body from side to side, then loops back around and repeats it. Now, the direction of that straight run is the clever part.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: On the vertical comb, straight up stands for the direction of the sun. So if the bee waggles at, say, forty degrees to the right of vertical, the food is forty degrees to the right of the sun. Not magnetic north, not the hive entrance. The sun.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: What about distance? A lot of students assume it's shown by how fast the bee shakes. Actually, the speed of the waggling hardly changes. It's the duration of the waggle run, how long it lasts, that tells the others how far to fly. So a longer run simply means a longer flight.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: As a rough guide, one second of waggling means the food's about 750 meters away. You'll see some books say a kilometer, but it varies between colonies, so treat it as approximate. Food two kilometers off might get a waggle run of nearly three seconds.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Now, remember it's pitch black inside a hive, so the other bees can't actually see any of this. Instead, they follow close behind the dancer, pick up the vibrations, and keep touching her body with their antennae. They also pick up the scent of the flowers she's been visiting, which helps them later on.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Right. So how do we know the dance really works like this? Von Frisch's evidence came from watching which feeding sites new bees turned up at. A stronger test came in the late 1980s, sorry, the early 1990s, when a team in Denmark built a robot bee. It was about the size of a real one, made of brass and driven by a computer. When it danced in the hive, real bees flew off to the spot its dance pointed to.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Another test used radar. Researchers fixed tiny transponders to bees that had just followed a dance, then tracked their flights across open fields. Most flew off in roughly the direction the dance had shown, although many still had to search around once they got there.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: There's also the question of how a bee measures distance in the first place. Researchers in Australia trained bees to fly down a narrow tunnel with patterned walls to reach food. Afterwards, the bees danced as if they'd flown many times farther than they really had. So they judge distance from how fast the world moves past their eyes, not from how tired they get.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Okay, finally, the limits. The dance is impressive, but it's not the whole story. When researchers watched hives closely, they found that a lot of experienced foragers ignore dances most of the time. They'd rather go back to places they know, relying on their memory of sites that worked before, along with smell.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: Other experiments deliberately scrambled the dance, by laying the comb flat and keeping the hive dark, so the direction information was lost. In many temperate habitats, those colonies collected about as much food as normal ones. The dance only made a clear difference where food comes in rare, rich patches, as in tropical forest.
turns.speaker: lecturer

turns.text: So the waggle dance is real, and it's remarkable. But it's one tool among several, and how much it matters depends on where the bees live. Next week, we'll see how ants solve the same problem using chemical trails.
turns.speaker: lecturer

groups.title: The honeybee waggle dance

questions.prompt: Von Frisch's method: bees trained to feed from a ______ of sugar water instead of real flowers
questions.evidence: he trained bees to visit a small dish of sugar water

explanation.uk: Лектор каже, що зі справжніми квітами було важко працювати, тож von Frisch використовував невелику мисочку з "sugar water" (цукровою водою), яку міг переставляти з місця на місце.

explanation.ru: Он думал о том, чтобы подрезать пчёлам крылья, но отказался от этой идеи: это изменило бы то, как они летают. Вместо этого он ставил на них точки краской ("paint").
explanation.uk: Він думав про те, щоб підрізати бджолам крила, але відмовився від цієї ідеї: це змінило б те, як вони літають. Натомість він ставив на них цятки фарбою ("paint").

questions.prompt: Dances watched in an observation hive with ______ sides
questions.evidence: a frame of comb with glass sides

explanation.en: An observation hive is a frame of comb with glass sides, so people can see inside without disturbing the bees.
explanation.ru: "Observation hive" — это рамка с сотами и стеклянными стенками ("glass"), поэтому можно заглянуть внутрь, не беспокоя пчёл.
explanation.uk: "Observation hive" — це рамка із сотами та скляними стінками ("glass"), тож можна зазирнути всередину, не турбуючи бджіл.

questions.prompt: Round dance: means the food is ______ to the hive
questions.evidence: If the food was close to the hive, within about fifty meters

explanation.en: The round dance is used when food is close to the hive, within about fifty meters. The waggle dance is used for food farther away.
explanation.ru: "Round dance" используется, когда корм находится близко к улью — примерно в пределах "fifty meters". "Waggle dance" — когда корм дальше.
explanation.uk: "Round dance" використовується, коли корм розташований близько до вулика — приблизно в межах "fifty meters". "Waggle dance" — коли корм далі.

questions.prompt: Waggle dance: angle of the straight run from vertical shows direction in relation to the ______
questions.evidence: straight up stands for the direction of the sun

explanation.en: Straight up on the comb stands for the sun's direction. The lecturer says it is not magnetic north or the hive entrance.
explanation.ru: Направление строго вверх по сотам обозначает направление на солнце ("sun"). Лектор уточняет, что это не магнитный север и не вход в улей.
explanation.uk: Напрямок точно вгору по сотах позначає напрямок на сонце ("sun"). Лектор уточнює, що це не магнітна північ і не вхід до вулика.

questions.prompt: Distance is shown by the ______ of the waggle run
questions.evidence: It's the duration of the waggle run, how long it lasts

explanation.en: Many students think the speed of shaking shows distance, but the lecturer says speed hardly changes. It is the duration, or how long the run lasts.
explanation.ru: Многие студенты думают, что расстояние показывает скорость покачиваний, но лектор говорит, что скорость почти не меняется. Важна "duration" — то есть сколько длится этот пробег.
explanation.uk: Багато студентів думають, що відстань показує швидкість похитувань, але лектор каже, що швидкість майже не змінюється. Важить "duration" — тобто скільки триває цей пробіг.

questions.prompt: One second of waggling ≈ food about ______ meters away
questions.evidence: one second of waggling means the food's about 750 meters away

explanation.en: One second means about 750 meters. A kilometer is what some books say, and two kilometers is a separate example.
explanation.ru: Одна секунда соответствует примерно "750" метрам. Километр — это то, что пишут в некоторых книгах, а два километра — отдельный пример.
explanation.uk: Одна секунда відповідає приблизно "750" метрам. Кілометр — це те, що пишуть у деяких книжках, а два кілометри — окремий приклад.

questions.prompt: Hive is dark, so followers stay in contact with the dancer using their ______
questions.evidence: keep touching her body with their antennae

explanation.en: The other bees can't see the dance in the dark, so they feel vibrations and keep touching the dancer with their antennae.
explanation.ru: В темноте другие пчёлы не видят танца, поэтому они ощущают вибрации ("vibrations") и постоянно касаются танцующей пчелы усиками ("antennae").
explanation.uk: У темряві інші бджоли не бачать танцю, тому вони відчувають вібрації ("vibrations") і постійно торкаються бджоли, що танцює, вусиками ("antennae").

questions.prompt: Danish team: a computer-driven ______ bee sent real bees to a chosen spot
questions.evidence: a team in Denmark built a robot bee

explanation.en: In the early 1990s, a team in Denmark built a robot bee made of brass and driven by a computer. Real bees flew where its dance pointed.
explanation.ru: В начале 1990-х команда в Дании ("Denmark") построила пчелу-робота из латуни ("brass"), которой управлял компьютер. Настоящие пчёлы летели туда, куда указывал её танец.
explanation.uk: На початку 1990-х команда в Данії ("Denmark") створила бджолу-робота з латуні ("brass"), якою керував комп'ютер. Справжні бджоли летіли туди, куди вказував її танець.

questions.prompt: Flights of bees that had followed a dance were tracked using ______
questions.evidence: Another test used radar.

explanation.en: Researchers put tiny transponders on bees and tracked them by radar. Most flew in roughly the direction the dance showed.
explanation.ru: Исследователи прикрепляли к пчёлам крошечные транспондеры ("transponders") и отслеживали их с помощью радара ("radar"). Большинство пчёл летели примерно в том направлении, которое показывал танец.
explanation.uk: Дослідники прикріплювали до бджіл крихітні транспондери ("transponders") і відстежували їх за допомогою радара ("radar"). Більшість бджіл летіли приблизно в тому напрямку, який показував танець.
